## Purpose

This lane reviews source identity, textual/semantic representation, and the software boundary between religious-text metadata and numerical physical computation.

It does not ask a reviewer to certify a religion, settle theology, or derive scientific constants from scripture.

## Review scope

### source_text_identity

Check that references identify the intended corpus/passage/source-language context and that translation provenance is not silently erased.

### semantic_vs_numerical_boundary

Check that concepts such as day/night, Sun, Moon, phases, months, years, reckoning, and appointed times remain semantic/textual metadata unless an independent physical model supplies numerical quantities.

### no_physics_injection

Check the hard rule that revelation records cannot inject hidden constants, correction coefficients, epochs, gear ratios, astronomical thresholds, or time-scale offsets into physical M-Time state.

### interpretation_uncertainty

Check that translation, interpretation, corpus differences, and scholarly disagreement are represented as uncertainty/review status rather than false machine certainty.

## Verdict boundary

A PASS means the reviewed metadata/boundary design is acceptably explicit under the reviewer's stated expertise and scope.

It does not make M-Time a religious authority, does not establish a universal jurisprudential rule, and does not permit scripture to bypass empirical validation of physical claims.
